one_liner: Header-only C++14 dense/sparse linear-algebra library with smart expression templates; claims Eigen/MKL-class speed, but no checkable numbers.
what_it_does: Blaze gives C++ a math DSL for dense and sparse vectors and matrices (StaticVector/Matrix, HybridVector/Matrix, DynamicVector/Matrix, CompressedVector/Matrix, views, symmetric/Hermitian/triangular adaptors), plus decompositions, solve(), eigen() and svd() through LAPACK. You write A*B+C as expressions; it is a different API from Eigen and from raw BLAS calls, not a drop-in for either.
how_it_is_fast: 'Smart expression templates': operators build expression objects that are dispatched at assignment to hand-written SIMD kernels (SSE through AVX-512/FMA, optional SLEEF or XSIMD), so it does not just fuse element-wise loops. Dense vectors and matrices are padded and aligned by default, so the kernels need no scalar remainder loops. Large dense products go through a blocked, packed mmm() kernel (blaze/math/dense/MMM.h copies K x N panels of A and B into temporaries) or, if BLAZE_BLAS_MODE is set, to cblas gemm. Shared-memory parallelism (OpenMP by default, or C++11/Boost threads or HPX) starts only above per-operation size thresholds in blaze/config/Thresholds.h.
when_to_use: Code that mixes dense and sparse vectors and matrices in one expression syntax (for example sparse matrix times dense vector inside an iterative solver)
Small and medium fixed-size or bounded-size algebra (StaticMatrix/HybridMatrix) where padding to the SIMD width is acceptable
HPC codes already on HPX: Blaze has an HPX parallel backend, and STEllAR's blaze_tensor and blaze_cuda extend it
Large dense products where you will link MKL or OpenBLAS anyway: BLAZE_BLAS_MODE routes gemm to the BLAS and keeps the expression syntax
when_not_to_use: If you need evidence that it beats Eigen or MKL: the Benchmarks wiki is unreachable, results quoted on HN date from 2016-17, and the one third-party benchmark found (Fastor wiki) has Blaze about 50% slower than Fastor and MKL JIT for small fixed-size products
Projects that need an active upstream: the last release is 3.8.2 (August 2020), and the stated compiler testing stops at GCC 10.2, Clang 10 and VS2017
Running several Blaze operations at once from different threads (OpenMP sections, task pools): the docs say Blaze 'does not support concurrent parallel computations', so you have to serialize them
Memory-tight code with many tiny matrices: padding makes aligned StaticVector/StaticMatrix larger than their elements, and zeroing the padding costs time
Builds without LAPACK: the CMake package does find_package(LAPACK REQUIRED) by default, and decompositions, inverse, eigen and svd fail to link without it

integration.dependencies: none for basic arithmetic; LAPACK for decompositions/inversion/eigen/svd (required by the default CMake config); optional BLAS (cblas.h), OpenMP, Boost.Thread, HPX, SLEEF, XSIMD
integration.min_toolchain: C++14 (cxx_std_14); README says it is tested with GCC 6.0-10.2, Clang 5.0-10.0 and Visual C++ 2017 (Win64 only)
integration.platforms: Any C++14 target; SIMD kernels for x86 SSE through AVX-512/FMA and SVML; other ISAs only through the optional XSIMD/SLEEF paths or scalar code
integration.thread_safety: Separate objects can be used from separate threads, but Blaze's own parallelization assumes one operation at a time: concurrent Blaze operations (e.g. in OpenMP sections) must be wrapped in serial() or run with parallelization disabled; BLAZE_SERIAL_SECTION is undefined behavior if used from several threads
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: it is not an Eigen API or BLAS ABI replacement, but BLAZE_BLAS_MODE lets it call your existing BLAS for gemm inside Blaze expressions

gotchas: Aliasing like x = A * x is detected and fixed with a temporary; noalias() turns this check off, and the docs warn that misuse is undefined behavior
Padding is on by default (BLAZE_USE_PADDING=1, blaze::padded); turning it off sends remainders to scalar code, which is what the Fastor benchmark saw
Thread counts come from BLAZE_NUM_THREADS or OMP_NUM_THREADS, or setNumThreads(); OpenMP is the default backend in CMake and drops silently to one thread (with a CMake warning) if OpenMP is not found
With BLAZE_BLAS_MODE, BLAZE_BLAS_IS_PARALLEL has to match the BLAS you link; otherwise Blaze threads and BLAS threads can oversubscribe the cores
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Choose Blaze over Eigen if you want one expression syntax over dense and sparse types and an HPX backend, and you can accept a stale upstream and no current evidence on speed; Eigen is the safer default and is the one with published, monitored numbers. For many tiny matrices, BLASFEO has measured wins over OpenBLAS and BLIS, which Blaze does not.
verified_claims_summary: No Blaze-vs-baseline number could be checked: the Bitbucket Benchmarks wiki returned 404, and the repo has only the Blazemark harness (switches for MKL/BLAS, Eigen, Armadillo, uBLAS, Blitz++, GMM++, FLENS, MTL), no results. The one third-party measurement opened (Fastor wiki; Blaze 3.7, GCC 7.4 -O3 with AVX-512 flags, Xeon Gold 6128, double, M=1-32, N=7/13/21/31, K=31) puts Blaze with padding at parity to over 2x slower than Fastor, about 50% slower on average, and generally behind MKL JIT.
status_note: Stale: last commit 2024-12-30 and no release since 3.8.2 (2020-08-15). It is BSD-3-Clause and header-only, ships as vcpkg and Conan packages, and is fine to vendor, but plan to maintain it yourself.
